text:
Predicates:
AllowedPetsIn(x, y) ::: Pets are allowed in building y.
DepositRequired(x, y) ::: A deposit is required to rent apartment x in building y.
DepositAmount(x, y, z) ::: The security deposit for apartment x in building y is z.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
Cats(x) ::: x is a cat.
Pets(x) ::: x is a pet.
ManagedBuilding(y) ::: y is a managed building.
Rent(x, y) ::: y is the monthly rent for apartment x.
RentAmount(x, y) ::: The rent amount for apartment x is y.
WillRent(x, y) ::: x will rent apartment y.
AllowedToMoveInWith(x, y) ::: x is allowed to move in with y.
Premises:
AllowedPetsIn(Fluffy, OliveGarden) ::: Pets are allowed in the Olive Garden.
DepositRequired(OliveGarden, x) ::: A deposit is required to rent in the Olive Garden.
Rent(OliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
∀x (Cats(x) → Pet(x)) ::: Cats are pets.
Tom is a pet (from context, but not explicitly predicate here).
Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
(AllowedToMoveInWith(Tom, Fluffy) ∧ DepositAmount(OliveGarden, 2000) ≤ 1500) → WillRent(Tom, OliveGarden)

Conclusion:
¬WillRent(Tom, OliveGarden)
